title: Silken Tofu with Soy Sauce and Scallions (Xiao Cong Ban Dou Fu)

source.name: Every Grain of Rice: Simple Chinese Home Cooking - Fuchsia Dunlop
source.location: Xiao Cong Ban Dou Fu Section

ingredients.name: chili oil or ground white pepper

steps: Carefully drain the silken tofu block and place on a shallow serving plate. Let stand for 5 minutes, then tip the plate to pour off any pooled liquid.
Using a small paring knife, gently score the tofu block into 1/2-inch cubes directly on the plate without disrupting the block's shape.
In a small ramekin, whisk together the light soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, and sugar until dissolved.
Scatter the finely sliced scallions generously over the entire surface of the tofu.
Drizzle the soy and sesame oil dressing evenly over the scallions and tofu. Serve immediately at cool room temperature with chopsticks or a flat spoon.
swaps: Soft tofu can replace silken tofu if silken is unavailable.
Chopped fresh cilantro or crushed roasted peanuts can be added as a garnish.
notes: A classic Chinese home-style cold dish highlighting the natural silky texture of high-quality unheated silken tofu.

title: Savory Lettuce Cups with Extra-Firm Tofu and Ground Beef

source.name: Our 50 Most-Popular Healthy Recipes - Food Network
source.location: Lettuce Cups with Tofu and Beef (Ellie Krieger)

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu, drained, pressed and finely diced
Bibb or Boston lettuce, leaves separated and rinsed

steps: Press the extra-firm tofu between paper towels with a heavy plate for 15 minutes, then cut into neat 1/4-inch dice.
Heat sesame oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking into crumbles, until no longer pink.
Add the minced garlic, grated ginger, and diced pressed tofu to the skillet. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the tofu lightly browns and absorbs the savory rendered pan drippings.
Stir in the hoisin sauce and soy sauce, tossing continuously for 2 minutes to coat the beef and tofu evenly in a glossy glaze.
Remove skillet from heat and stir in the chopped scallions.
Spoon generous mounds of the warm filling into crisp Bibb lettuce cups. Drizzle lightly with chili-garlic sauce and serve immediately.
swaps: Ground turkey or chicken can substitute for ground beef.
Diced water chestnuts or finely chopped celery can be added for extra crunch.
notes: Combining pressed extra-firm tofu with lean meat produces a satisfying, low-fat protein filling that absorbs aromatic hoisin and soy sauces.

title: Crispy Air-Fryer Tofu Larb with Fresh Herbs and Lime

source.name: The Complete Veggie Air Fryer Cookbook

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
soy sauce or vegetarian fish sauce

steps: Preheat the air fryer to 400°F (200°C). Toss the pressed tofu cubes with oil, cornstarch, and a pinch of salt until lightly coated.
Arrange the tofu in a single layer in the air fryer basket. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through, until deep golden and crisp.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the lime juice, soy sauce, and chili flakes.
Transfer the hot crispy tofu directly into the bowl with the dressing. Add the sliced shallots, torn mint, and fresh cilantro.
Toss quickly to coat the tofu while keeping its exterior crunch. Sprinkle with toasted ground rice powder and serve immediately with raw cabbage wedges or steamed sticky rice.
swaps: Scallions can replace shallots if unavailable.
Crushed toasted peanuts can substitute for toasted rice powder for nutty texture.
notes: Air-frying gives pressed tofu a shatter-crisp surface that absorbs the tangy lime and chili dressing without turning soggy.

title: Hearty Golden Tofu Scramble with Vegetables

source.name: Frugal Vegan - Katie Koteen & Kate Kasbee

steps: Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the diced bell pepper and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Crumble the drained tofu into the skillet using your hands, creating bite-sized rustic curds.
Sprinkle turmeric, garlic powder, nutritional yeast, black pepper, and salt evenly over the crumbled tofu.
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently with a spatula, for 5 to 6 minutes until excess moisture cooks off and curds are hot and evenly colored.
Fold in the baby spinach and sliced scallions during the final minute of cooking, stirring just until the spinach wilts. Serve hot with whole-grain toast or roasted potatoes.
swaps: Mushrooms or diced zucchini can be sautéed alongside the bell peppers.
A pinch of black salt (kala namak) can be added for authentic egg flavor.
notes: A quick, protein-packed breakfast or dinner skillet that mimics the appearance and mouthfeel of soft scrambled eggs using basic pantry spices.

title: Crisp Tofu and Green Bean Stir-Fry with Crushed Peanuts

source.name: Recipes - The Nutrition Source (Harvard T.H. Chan)
source.location: Nut, Bean, and Tofu Recipe Series

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
fresh green beans, trimmed and halved

steps: Press tofu cubes thoroughly between paper towels for 15 minutes to dry surfaces.

Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the tofu cubes and sear for 6 to 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden-crisp on all sides; remove to a plate.
Add the trimmed green beans and 2 tablespoons of water to the pan. Cover with a lid and steam for 3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Uncover, add minced garlic and ginger, and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared tofu to the pan. Pour in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil, tossing over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes until sauce glazes the vegetables and tofu.
Remove from heat, transfer to a platter, and top generously with crushed roasted peanuts before serving with steamed brown rice.
swaps: Snap peas or broccoli florets can replace green beans.
Cashews or toasted sesame seeds can substitute for peanuts.
notes: Blends crisp seared plant protein with crunchy steamed green beans and heart-healthy roasted peanuts in a light savory sauce.
